title: Delegates, lambdas and events

notes: Func<int, int> holds a function from int to int; the lambda x => x * 2 is one.
Action<string> takes a string and returns nothing.
Health doesn't know about health bars or sounds; it only raises events.
?.Invoke skips the call when nobody has subscribed.
The second Damage reaches 0, so both Changed and Died fire.

exercises.title: Passing behaviour
exercises.prompt:
In static class Rules write (with your own loops, no LINQ Select):
- List<int> Apply(List<int> values, Func<int, int> change): a new list with change applied to each value.
- int CountWhere(List<int> values, Func<int, bool> test): how many pass the test.
- Func<int, int> Multiplier(int factor): returns a function that multiplies by factor.
- void Repeat(int times, Action<int> action): calls action(1), action(2) ... action(times).

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var seen = new List<string>(); Rules.Repeat(3, i => seen.Add("wave " + i)); return string.Join(", ", seen); }))()
tests.name: repeat an action

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var log = new List<int>(); Rules.Repeat(0, i => log.Add(i)); return log.Count + " " + Rules.Multiplier(0)(99); }))()
tests.name: zero times, times zero

tests.why: Write the loop yourself here, so you see what LINQ does inside.

hints: Apply: var result = new List<int>(); foreach (int v in values) result.Add(change(v)); return result;
public static Func<int, int> Multiplier(int factor) => x => x * factor;
public static void Repeat(int times, Action<int> action) { for (int i = 1; i <= times; i++) action(i); }

exercises.title: Health that announces changes
exercises.prompt:
Finish class Health with two events: `public event Action<int> Changed;` (gets the new value) and `public event Action Died;`.
- Damage(int amount) and Heal(int amount): a negative amount throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Current stays between 0 and Max.
- Raise Changed only if Current really changed (healing at full health stays quiet).
- Raise Died once, when Current reaches 0. Once dead, Damage and Heal do nothing.
- It must not crash when nobody is listening.

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var h = new Health(100); var log = new List<int>(); h.Changed += v => log.Add(v); h.Damage(30); h.Heal(10); return string.Join(",", log); }))()
tests.name: changes are announced

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var h = new Health(20); int deaths = 0; h.Died += () => deaths++; h.Damage(15); h.Damage(15); h.Damage(15); return deaths + " " + h.Current; }))()
tests.name: dies once

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var h = new Health(10); h.Damage(5); return "no listeners ok " + h.Current; }))()
tests.name: nobody listening
tests.hint_if_fail: Use Changed?.Invoke(Current) so it's safe with no subscribers.

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var h = new Health(50); int calls = 0; h.Changed += v => calls++; h.Heal(10); h.Damage(0); h.Damage(5); return calls.ToString(); }))()
tests.name: no change, no event

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var h = new Health(10); var log = new List<int>(); h.Changed += v => log.Add(v); h.Damage(10); h.Heal(5); return string.Join(",", log) + " " + h.Current; }))()
tests.name: dead stays dead

hints: public event Action<int> Changed; public event Action Died;
Write one private method SetCurrent(int value) that both Damage and Heal call: clamp, compare, then raise.
if (Current == 0) return; int v = Math.Clamp(value, 0, Max); if (v == Current) return; Current = v; Changed?.Invoke(Current); if (Current == 0) Died?.Invoke();

exercises.title: Wave cleared (EventHandler<T>)
exercises.prompt:
WaveClearedEventArgs is given. In WaveManager:
- declare `public event EventHandler<WaveClearedEventArgs> WaveCleared;`
- StartWave(int enemies): fewer than 1 throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException; starting while enemies remain throws InvalidOperationException. Otherwise Wave goes up by 1 and Remaining = enemies.
- EnemyKilled(int points): with no enemies remaining throws InvalidOperationException. Otherwise Remaining goes down, the points add to this wave's score and to TotalScore. When Remaining reaches 0, raise WaveCleared with this WaveManager as the sender and (wave number, this wave's score).

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var w = new WaveManager(); var log = new List<string>(); w.WaveCleared += (s, e) => log.Add($"wave {e.Wave}: {e.Score}"); w.StartWave(2); w.EnemyKilled(10); w.EnemyKilled(15); w.StartWave(1); w.EnemyKilled(50); return string.Join(" | ", log) + " total " + w.TotalScore; }))()
tests.name: two waves

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var w = new WaveManager(); int n = 0; w.WaveCleared += (s, e) => n++; w.StartWave(3); w.EnemyKilled(1); w.EnemyKilled(1); return n + " " + w.Remaining; }))()
tests.name: not cleared yet

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var w = new WaveManager(); object sender = null; w.WaveCleared += (s, e) => sender = s; w.StartWave(1); w.EnemyKilled(5); return ReferenceEquals(sender, w).ToString(); }))()
tests.name: the sender is the manager

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var w = new WaveManager(); w.StartWave(2); w.StartWave(2); return "no error"; }))()
tests.name: can't start a wave mid-wave

hints: Keep a private int waveScore; reset it in StartWave.
In EnemyKilled, after updating the numbers: if (Remaining == 0) WaveCleared?.Invoke(this, new WaveClearedEventArgs(Wave, waveScore));
`this` is the sender: handlers get (object sender, WaveClearedEventArgs e).

quiz.q: What type holds a function that takes an int and returns a bool?
quiz.why: Func's last type is the return type.

quiz.q: Changed(Current); with no subscribers does what?
Why should Health raise an event instead of calling healthBar.Refresh() directly?
choices: Health stays independent; any number of parts can listen without Health knowing them
quiz.why: Loose coupling: announce, don't call around.

quiz.q: What does the `event` keyword stop outside code from doing?
choices: Firing the event or replacing all the listeners
A function that multiplies its input by 3
quiz.why: Functions can be returned like any value.

cards.a: Func returns a value (last type); Action returns nothing
event EventHandler<TArgs> Name; handlers get (object sender, TArgs e)

explain: Explain events in your own words, with an example of a game or app where several parts need to react to one thing happening.
